files.source: machine B (m1-16g), session 2026-09-12 — Letter 016 queue item 2
files.notes: run-on: m1-16g (Apple M1, 16 GB) · python 3.11.16 · torch 2.14.0 · numpy 2.4.6 · scipy 1.17.1 · device cpu, torch.set_num_threads(1), use_deterministic_algorithms(True) (B-env.json). Equipment Sarcos@b22f1e9 on branch bench-B-step0; main stays at fb37e04. · Letter 011 §2 Step 0 dose–response on the selected architecture, block-level builder, canonical split (blk 256, .8/.1/.1), seeds 13/14/15, ALL arms at the base's own ep60 (no ep300-vs-ep60 confound), doses {0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}, rank rows 4/4/4 · 16/16/7 · 21/21/7. VERDICT: NO DOSE QUALIFIES. learnability ratio scratch/FT (mean of 3 seeds): 9.53 / 5.54 / 5.60 / 4.30 at doses .25/.5/.75/1 — the registered fence (≤2×) is never met and the trend is monotone toward, not past, it: the arena closes as the shift is removed, i.e. the shift is not what makes the region unlearnable. far=0.1 is UNRUNNABLE under the registered rule: the builder returns 512 fit rows and 0 select rows, so best-on-select checkpointing is undefined — reported as such, no fallback invented (law 5). The floor also survives the schedule fix: frozen beats full-FT at every runnable dose (Δ = +0.0045/+0.0024/+0.0021/+0.0019). Exploratory calibration, not a hypothesis test; H9-S remains unregistered here.

Equipment Sarcos@b22f1e9 on branch bench-B-step0; main stays at fb37e04. · A check on bytes that already exist, not a new test (law 5). Letter 011 §1 files shift_summary_exploratory.json (16b95129…) as produced by the superseded ROW-LEVEL builder. B recomputed both geometries' downstream score at far=0.5 for the same deterministic bases: the exploratory FROZEN row (0.01952 / 0.03003) matches the BLOCK-level geometry to 1e-5 on both arches and misses the row-level reconstruction by 0.0029 / 0.0041. Mechanism named in the file: report.py::frozen_base_rows reads shift_eval.json, written on demand by `evaluate --eval-task shift` with whatever builder is committed TODAY, while shift_rows reads each arm's training-time metrics — one table, two vintages. Consequence for the record, not for the verdict: Letter 009's floor table compares a block-level frozen score against row-level arm scores. The floor itself stands (see the two dose files). Bonus measurement: B reproduces A's frozen row to 1e-5 across machines — the programme's first A-vs-B replication, machine effect at or below rounding.
